statement:
The starred arithmetic centralizer assertion}
Fix $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ and write $G_{\mathbf Q}$ for its full
profinite Galois group. For every open subgroup $\Gamma'\subset G_{\mathbf Q}$,
let $\Gamma'^{\circ}$ be the kernel of its cyclotomic character. Then
\[
 C_{G_{\mathbf Q}}(\Gamma'^{\circ})=1.
\]
\passage{Cote 149, \S2, manuscript p.~22, scan 45, starred ``\`a v\'erifier !''.}

statement:
The local extension and the normalizer correction}
Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\mathbf Q$, let
$U=X\setminus D$ be a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve,
and let $c\in D(K)$. Choose a geometric base point and a lift of $c$
to the normalized universal covering. Its inertia $I_c$ and
decomposition group $D_c$ satisfy
\[
 D_c=N_{E_U}(I_c),\qquad
 1\longrightarrow I_c=\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1)
 \longrightarrow D_c\longrightarrow G_K\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 C_{E_U}(I_c)=D_c\cap p^{-1}(\ker\chi_K).
\]
A local parameter supplies a splitting. The $I_c$-conjugacy classes of
splittings form a torsor under
$H^1(K,\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1))=\varprojlim_n K^*/K^{*n}$.
\passage{Cote 149, \S3, manuscript p.~26 and continuation, scans 53--54, formulas (2)--(3).}

statement:
Embedded, disjoint cusp packets, including type $(0,3)$}
Under the hypotheses of F10a the map from local splitting classes to
$\pi_1(U_{\overline K})$-conjugacy classes of sections of $E_U\to G_K$
is injective. Its image is disjoint from the classes of points of
$U(K)$ and from every other rational cusp packet. These assertions
hold after each finite extension of $K$.
\passage{Cote 149, \S3, manuscript pp.~26--27, scans 54--55, Proposition and its margin.}

statement:
The first assertion of scan 54 in type $(0,2)$}
For $U=\mathbf G_{m,K}$ each of the two rational cusp packets equals
the entire set of section classes, and in particular contains every
point section. The first assertion of scan 54 is therefore false in
this type. For every affine characteristic-zero type with nontrivial
geometric fundamental group, the disjointness conclusion holds exactly
in the hyperbolic cases covered by F10b.
\passage{Cote 149, \S3, continuation of manuscript p.~26, scan 54.}
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None
notes: Type (0,2) is an explicit failure of disjointness of point and cusp packets.

statement:
Local form and invariant complex structure}
A nonidentity orientation-preserving finite-order homeomorphism of a
connected surface has isolated fixed points, each with fixed-point index
$+1$. A cyclic finite group acting by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms
on a surface of finite type preserves a complex structure of a smooth
algebraic curve of that type.
\passage{Cote 142, opening, continuation of manuscript p.~1 (scan 6), and p.~3 (scan 7). The reading order is 4, 6, 5, 7.}

statement:
Periodic homological rigidity, with the level-two exception}
For a hyperbolic surface $S$, a finite-order homeomorphism acting trivially
on $H_1(S,\mathbf Z)$ is the identity. The same conclusion follows from
trivial action on $H_1(S,\mathbf Z/n)$ for any $n\geq3$. In particular,
a periodic homeomorphism isotopic to the identity is the identity.
The assertion with $n=2$ is false: $z\mapsto-z$ on
$(\mathbf R^2/\mathbf Z^2)\setminus\{0\}$ is a counterexample of type
$(1,1)$.
\passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript p.~2, scan 5; continuation p.~3, scan 7.}

statement:
Components, stabilizers, and the finiteness of covering orbits}
Let $X,Y$ be connected hyperbolic finite-type surfaces. In the space of
orientation-preserving finite covering maps $X\to Y$, each connected component
is homeomorphic to $A_0(X)$ and is contractible. Its isotopy class has
stabilizer, under precomposition by $M(X)$, exactly the finite deck group
of that covering, embedded by its mapping classes. There are finitely
many $M(X)$-orbits of isotopy classes. As the target $Y$ varies, a finite
subgroup of $M(X)$ occurs as such a stabilizer exactly when it has a
free realization on $X$ by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms.
\passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript pp.~1--3, scans 3,4,6--8.}

statement:
Hausdorff profinite envelope under the finite-index condition}
For every small $C_0$ satisfying the preceding finite-index condition
there is a category $\widehat C_0$ with the same objects and
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}_{\widehat C_0}(X,Y)=
 \coprod_{uA_X\in\operatorname{Hom}_{C_0}(X,Y)/A_X}
       \overline{S_u}\backslash\widehat A_X.                 \tag{G.1}
\]
Its Hom spaces are locally compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected;
composition is continuous and associative, and extends composition in
$C_0$. Each double orbit also equals the quotient of
$\widehat A_X\times\widehat A_Y$ by the closure of $G_u$, with the
opposite-action convention dictated by $bu=ua$.
The functor $C_0\to\widehat C_0$ has dense image in each Hom space.
It is conservative, and
\[
 \operatorname{Isom}_{\widehat C_0}(X,Y)=
 \operatorname{Isom}_{C_0}(X,Y)
       \mathop{\times}^{A_X}\widehat A_X,
 \qquad \operatorname{Aut}_{\widehat C_0}(X)=\widehat A_X.     \tag{G.2}
\]
The displayed contracted product for isomorphisms is a torsor product,
so no closure correction is needed there. Among Hausdorff topological
categories with continuous composition and profinite automorphism
groups, every functor from $C_0$ extends uniquely to a continuous functor
from this envelope whenever the target Hom topology induces its stated
profinite automorphism-group topology. This characterizes the envelope
up to a unique isomorphism fixing $C_0$.
\passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript pp.~4--6, scans 9--12 and 14; formulas (12)--(17), NB of scan 11, and conservativity NB of scan 14.}

statement:
The surface category and the marked-factorization assertion}
The isotopy category of orientation-preserving finite covers of connected
hyperbolic surfaces satisfies the condition of G6. Its finite deck groups
embed in the profinite completions of the source mapping-class groups.
For this category, $\widehat G_u\to\widehat M(X)\times\widehat M(Y)$
is injective and its image is the arrow stabilizer.
Every completed arrow has a factorization $u\widehat f_0$, where $u$
is an original finite cover and $\widehat f_0$ a completed isomorphism;
the resulting \emph{marked factorization} is determined up to a unique
original isomorphism over the target.
\passage{Cote 142, opening, manuscript pp.~5--6, scans 11 and 14.}

statement:
The category with already profinite automorphism groups}
Let $C$ be a small category with profinite automorphism groups $A_X$.
For every arrow $u:X\to Y$, suppose that
$G_u=\{(a,b):bu=ua\}$ is closed in $A_X\times A_Y$ and its image
$H_u$ in $A_Y$ has finite index. Give each double orbit its compact
quotient topology, and give each Hom set the disjoint union topology.
Composition is continuous. The image $H_u$ is closed and open, and the
right $A_X$-orbits are open in each double orbit.
\passage{Cote 142, manuscript pp.~4--5, scans 10--11, especially (14)--(16).}

statement:
The doubtful homology qualification in scan 5}
For orientation-preserving periodic homeomorphisms of a hyperbolic
finite-type surface, trivial action on ordinary $H_1$ or on
Borel--Moore $H_1$ with integral coefficients implies the identity.
The same is true with coefficients $\mathbf Z/n$, $n\geq3$.
Without the orientation-preserving hypothesis, still for periodic
homeomorphisms, the Borel--Moore version is false, whereas the ordinary
version remains G2. Replacing either by the
homology of the compactification alone is also false.
\passage{Cote 142, manuscript p.~2, scan 5: the doubtful word following $H_1$, transcribed as ``propre''.}

statement:
Orientation signs and compactness of the Hom spaces}
For the full, possibly orientation-reversing, finite-cover isotopy
category, the orbits under $M^+(X)$ are indexed by
$R_X(Y)\times\{+1,-1\}$, where $R_X(Y)$ is the finite set of
unoriented isomorphism classes of covers of $Y$ homeomorphic to $X$.
In the oriented completed category, each Hom space is compact and
metrizable. The unqualified assertion that it has no isolated points
is false: for $X=Y=\mathbf P^1(\mathbf C)\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$
the Hom space consists of the six elements of $S_3$. With individually
labelled punctures it consists of one element. More generally, a
nonempty completed right orbit has no isolated points exactly when
$\widehat{M^+(X)}$ is infinite.
\passage{Cote 142, manuscript pp.~3--6, scans 8--9 and 13.}

statement:
The characteristic-zero algebraic category and its comparison}
Over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero there is
a category $\mathcal T_k$ described by the following arrows:
\[
 X\longrightarrow Y:\quad
 (u:X'\longrightarrow Y,\ \alpha:X\rightsquigarrow X'
                         \text{ in }\Pi_1^{\acute et}(\mathcal M_a)),
                                                               \tag{Z.2}
\]
modulo isomorphisms of finite covers that carry the marking $\alpha$
to the other marking. Composition transports the first cover along
the second marking using (Z.1), and then composes the finite maps.
Over $\mathbf C$ this category is naturally equivalent, with its
profinite Hom topologies, to the category of G8 restricted to complex
algebraic curves. Base extension along any embedding $k\hookrightarrow
k'$ of algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields induces an
equivalence $\mathcal T_k\to\mathcal T_{k'}$. Its object isomorphism
classes are precisely the hyperbolic types $(g,n)$, and its
automorphism group at a complex object is the full profinite
completion of the oriented mapping-class group.
\passage{Cote 142, manuscript pp.~6--7, scans 13--16.}

statement:
The positive-characteristic base-invariance premise}
The assertion on scan 16 that the full geometric fundamental group
of a curve is invariant under every extension of algebraically closed
fields is false in characteristic $p>0$. The counterexample already
occurs on the hyperbolic curve
$U=\mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$.
The valid replacements are: invariance for curves in characteristic
zero; invariance for proper curves in arbitrary characteristic; and
invariance of the maximal prime-to-$p$ geometric fundamental group
of a smooth curve in characteristic $p$.
\passage{Cote 142, manuscript p.~7, scans 15--16, parenthetical justification.}

statement:
Field automorphisms and the actual outer ambiguity}
Every automorphism $\sigma$ of an algebraically closed characteristic-zero
field $k$ induces a functor on $\mathcal T_k$ by base change, and these
functors compose with their canonical base-change isomorphisms. After
choosing one object of each type and paths to its conjugates, the
induced automorphisms of its profinite automorphism group are defined
up to inner automorphisms. Changing a path by $a$ changes the induced
automorphism by conjugation by $a$.
\passage{Cote 142, manuscript pp.~7--8, scans 16--17.}
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None
notes: Explicit base-change functors and inner ambiguity of their action on a skeleton.

statement:
Path isotopy after allowing extra omitted branch points}
For maps obtained by composing finite covers and inclusions that fill
punctures, a continuous path through \'etale maps need not lie in a
single two-sided orbit of the identity components of the source and
target homeomorphism groups. The following example is an explicit
composite of the two allowed sorts of arrows, has degree six,
and has fixed source type $(0,20)$ and target type $(0,3)$.
For a continuous family of holomorphic maps of compact curves with
fixed ramification data and fixed incidence partition of the images
of all marked points, local path isotopies do lie in such a two-sided
orbit. The incidence hypothesis is essential in the example.
\passage{Cote 142, manuscript pp.~8--9, scans 18--19; ``isotopie raisonnable''.}

statement:
Filling punctures and the necessary source containment}
For finite maps $\overline f:\overline X\to\overline Y$ of smooth
proper curves in characteristic zero, and finite reduced sets $S,T$,
the restriction $X=\overline X\setminus S\to
Y=\overline Y\setminus T$ is defined and \'etale exactly when
$\overline f^{-1}(T)\subset S$ and every ramification point of
$\overline f$ lies in $S$. Composing finite \'etale maps and puncture
fillings produces such maps, including maps whose omitted
ramification points have images inside $Y$.
For ordered punctures, forgetting a specified set $I$ induces a
functor on \'etale fundamental groupoids of the corresponding moduli
stacks whenever the remaining type is hyperbolic. Successive
forgettings compose with their canonical natural isomorphisms.
\passage{Cote 142, manuscript pp.~8--10, scans 18, 20--21.}
